summary: iter43 backend-only verification of the legacy pro_expires_at fallback in _is_pro() + /me/subscription, and the new one-shot POST /api/admin/promo/migrate-legacy endpoint. Wrote 9 new tests in test_legacy_pro_migration.py hand-injecting the legacy field via direct pymongo writes against the local Mongo (the preview URL cannot be used for these tests because it routes to a Mongo we cannot touch — see context_for_next_testing_agent). ALL 9 NEW TESTS PASS. ALL 14 iter41+42 promo_redeem regression tests still pass (test_promo_redeem.py: 14/14). Verified: (a) legacy field in future -> pro=true / plan=pro / days_left ~30; (b) legacy field in past -> pro=false / days_left=0; (c) Zulu 'Z' suffix parsed correctly; (d) free-tier 3-session cap lifted for legacy-pro user (5 saves succeed, no 402); (e) non-admin gets 403 on migrate-legacy; (f) admin migration promotes legacy user (pro_until=pro_expires_at, plan='pro', pro_source='promo:legacy' when empty); (g) canonical (pro_until-already-set) users untouched — pro_until/plan/pro_source byte-identical after migration; (h) idempotency — second migration run returns migrated=0; (i) pro_source is preserved when already set (only fills 'promo:legacy' when empty); (j) fresh WELCOME30 redemption continues to write canonical pro_until (no regression).
verified_backend_expectations: _is_pro() honors legacy pro_expires_at when pro_until missing
_is_pro() parses ISO with 'Z' Zulu suffix without crashing
/me/subscription returns pro=true/plan=pro/days_left=30 from legacy field alone
/api/sessions cap lifted for legacy-pro user (5x saves OK)
POST /admin/promo/migrate-legacy shape: {ok, migrated: int, scanned: int}
Migration writes pro_until=pro_expires_at, plan=pro, pro_source='promo:legacy' (only when empty)
Migration does NOT touch users with pro_until already set (canonical untouched)
Migration preserves existing pro_source (e.g. 'promo:TRYME' not overwritten)
critical_code_review_comments: server.py L2717: migration query uses {"pro_until": {"$in": [None, ""]}} which correctly matches missing OR null OR empty-string. Confirmed working. Note: users where pro_until key is entirely absent are also matched because MongoDB $in with null matches missing fields. Verified via idempotency test.

server.py L563 _is_pro(): the exception-swallowing `except Exception: continue` is fine defensively but silently masks malformed datetime strings. If a bad string enters the DB, users may quietly lose Pro access with no log line. Consider a debug log inside the except.

server.py L742 days_left calc: `delta.days + (1 if delta.seconds > 0 else 0)` for future dates gives inclusive rounding but for a value 30 days in future the .days may show 29 with .seconds > 0 -> yielding 30. Confirmed correct via test (accepts 29 or 30). For a Zulu-suffix input we verified round-trip works.

context_for_next_testing_agent: IMPORTANT: test_legacy_pro_migration.py hits http://localhost:8001 directly (NOT the preview REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL). Reason: the test hand-injects the legacy `pro_expires_at` field via direct pymongo write into MONGO_URL from backend/.env — that Mongo is only shared with the local backend. If you need to run these tests against a different backend, set the BACKEND_TEST_URL env var AND ensure MONGO_URL points to the same Mongo the target backend uses. Also note EmailStr lowercases emails on register — always use lowercase 'test_' prefix (NOT 'TEST_') when doing direct Mongo lookups.
rca of the issue: Prod user prestonebyrd@gmail.com redeemed WELCOME30/TRYME under the pre-iter41 code path which wrote the entitlement to `pro_expires_at` + `pro_status` but not the canonical `pro_until`. iter41's `_is_pro()` only reads `pro_until`, so the user's DB record silently made them look free-tier. The iter43 fix: (1) `_is_pro()` and `/me/subscription` now iterate over ('pro_until','pro_expires_at') and use the first present, non-expired value — historical redemptions are unlocked live with no DB touch; (2) `.replace('Z','+00:00')` on both parse paths hardens against Zulu-suffix ISO strings that older Mongo drivers/paths may have serialised; (3) POST /api/admin/promo/migrate-legacy is a one-shot idempotent cleanup that promotes stale records to the canonical schema so downstream code that reads only `pro_until` (e.g. analytics, exports) also picks them up. Verified all three code paths behave as expected and no regression to canonical flow.
